bundle.author: jagoda
bundle.title: Wire break-glass approval to a real grant (sheriff step 4)
bundle.body:
Step 4 of `docs/sheriff.md`: wire the break-glass approval to a real grant, with
the two engineer-decided changes from the settled design (email mapping instead
of the hardcoded Slack-id map, and an `Engineers` membership gate at request
time).

## What changed

**Request-time identity resolution and the `Engineers` gate** (`sheriff/handler.ts`,
`sheriff/identity.ts`, `sheriff/policy.ts`)

- `slack.users.info` -> `user.profile.email`; `identitystore:GetUserId` on
  `emails.value`; `identitystore:IsMemberInGroups` against the `Engineers` group
  (`383193a0-7001-70d9-a321-ffe6d8af7378`). Only then is a `requested` record
  written, stamped with `requesterIdentityStoreId` and `requesterEmail`.
- The three misses are distinct inline `response_action: "errors"` messages
  keyed to `reason_block`: no Slack email, no Identity Center user for that
  email, not an `Engineers` member. No DMs. No negative cache.
- The hardcoded `SLACK_TO_IDENTITY_STORE_USER_ID` map is deleted from
  `sheriff/config.ts`.

**The real grant path** (`sheriff/handler.ts`, `sheriff/policy.ts`, `sheriff/store.ts`)

- The dry-run `approved` state is gone. On approve: a race-safe conditional
  write claims a per-requester active-grant lock (`attribute_not_exists(pk) OR
  state = released`); a request already having an active grant gets the
  "already active" ephemeral and stops. Then the request moves to `granting`,
  the grant record is written in `granting`, `CreateGroupMembership` is called,
  and the record flips to `granted` with the `membershipId`.
- `ConflictException` resolves the existing `MembershipId` with
  `ListGroupMembershipsForMember` (matched on `Admins`), falling back to the
  group listing if the member-scoped listing lags. Any other error -> `failed`,
  lock released, failure posted, no access.
- The granted copy links the SSO portal and states the session caveat: the
  `administrator` set is `PT1H`, so sign out and back in, and the honest worst
  case is the requested duration plus the remaining session.

**Application audit** (`sheriff/handler.ts`)

- One `console.log(JSON.stringify({ audit, ... }))` per transition:
  `request.created`, `request.approved`, `request.denied`, `grant.created`,
  `grant.revoked`, `grant.failed`, `membership.orphaned`, plus
  `membership.unmanaged` from the sweeper. Each carries request id, requester,
  approver, group, reason, ticket and timestamps where applicable.
  `grant.created` is informational, not paging.

**Sweeper and alarm** (`sheriff/handler.ts`, `sheriff-lambda.ts`)

- A periodic EventBridge rule (`rate(5 minutes)`) invokes the same Lambda with
  `{ action: "sweep" }`. It lists `Admins`, queries the tool's grant records,
  and reconciles: `granting` + no member -> `failed` (no alarm); `granting` +
  member -> backfill `membershipId`, flip to `granted`, revoke if expired;
  expired `granted` -> revoke and mark `revoked`; a member with no active grant
  record -> `membership.unmanaged`, informational, never touched.
- **In-flight guard.** A `granting` record younger than a 5-minute grace window
  is left alone. The async approve path may still be running, and failing the
  record now would strand the membership that lands afterwards (Bugbot's
  "standing admin" case). A record that is genuinely stuck ages past the window
  and is reconciled on a later sweep.
- **Conditional transitions.** Every sweeper state write is conditional on the
  state the plan saw, so a record the approve path moved mid-sweep is not
  clobbered. A skipped write also skips the lock release.
- A log metric filter on `{ $.audit = "membership.orphaned" }` feeds a
  `Sheriff/MembershipOrphaned` alarm that targets a new `sheriff-alerts` SNS
  topic (`aws-infrastructure@goodparty.org`), with an SNS topic policy letting
  `cloudwatch.amazonaws.com` publish.

**The Slack 3-second ack budget** (`sheriff/handler.ts`, `sheriff-lambda.ts`)

Slack requires an HTTP 200 within 3 seconds for `block_actions` and
`view_submission`. The synchronous handlers now do only the fast work and hand
the slow work to an asynchronous self-invocation of the same function
(`InvocationType: "Event"`):

- `view_submission` keeps the eligibility gate inline — the engineer explicitly
  wants the inline `response_action: "errors"` feedback — writes the `requested`
  record, then async-posts the approval message and returns `clear`. If the
  async invocation fails to start, it falls back to posting inline rather than
  losing the request.
- `block_actions` checks the clicker and the request, then async-decides and
  returns immediately. The async `decide` handler re-fetches the request,
  re-runs `evaluateDecision`, and performs the grant.
- The Lambda role gains `lambda:InvokeFunction` on its own ARN only.

The async paths are idempotent, so a Slack retry cannot double-grant: the async
`decide` re-runs `evaluateDecision` and stops on a request that is no longer
`requested`; the active-grant lock's conditional claim is the race-safe
backstop; and `activeGrantDecision` distinguishes our own retry (silent) from a
different active grant (the "already active" ephemeral). The at-most-one guard
and the eligibility gate are unchanged.

**IAM** (`deploy/components/sheriff-grant.ts`, `deploy-infrastructure/sheriff-lambda.ts`)

- `sheriff-grant` gains `identitystore:GetUserId` (identity store + user
  wildcard) and `identitystore:IsMemberInGroups` (Engineers group + identity
  store + user + membership wildcard). `ListUsers`, `DescribeUser`,
  `DescribeGroup`, `sso:*` and `sso-directory:*` stay absent.
- The Lambda role gains `sts:AssumeRole` on exactly
  `arn:aws:iam::333022194791:role/sheriff-grant`, `dynamodb:Query`, and
  `lambda:InvokeFunction` on its own ARN. It still holds **no** `identitystore`
  action of its own.

**Docs** (`docs/sheriff.md`)

- Open question 3 is now settled as email mapping + the `Engineers` gate; the
  "unchanged from step 2" line for the grant role is corrected. The Goal
  invariant reads "any member of `Engineers` can request admin". Step 3 is
  `done`, step 4 `doing`. The state machine and orphaned wording are reconciled
  with the sweeper-only revoke path.

**Config**

- `APPROVER_SLACK_USER_IDS` is now exactly `["U0BMU0DPS9Y"]` — Jeff Jagoda
  (`jeff@goodparty.org`), the engineer, deliberately the only approver for now,
  changed only by a reviewed PR. The previous placeholder is gone.
- Adds `@aws-sdk/client-identitystore` and `@aws-sdk/client-lambda`.

## The revoke-path decision

Step 4 deliberately has **no one-shot scheduler**; that is step 5. The periodic
sweeper is the revoke path, so every expired grant is revoked on the next pass.
The definition of `orphaned` is therefore: an expired grant whose member is
still present **after** the sweeper's revoke attempt — the revoke failed or the
state is stuck. A normal sweep-and-revoke is expected and silent; only a failed
revoke emits `membership.orphaned` and pages. `docs/sheriff.md` is updated to
say this.

## Verification

```
$ npx tsc --noEmit                                  # clean
$ npx tsc --noEmit -p deploy-infrastructure/tsconfig.json   # clean
$ npm test
# tests 356
# suites 81
# pass 356
# fail 0
```

New tests cover: the three eligibility failure modes (pure), the
at-most-one-active-grant conditional (condition expression and the failed-claim
path), the sweeper's grace window and every other reconciliation case, the
conditional sweeper transitions, `activeGrantDecision` (own retry vs another
grant), `granting -> granted`, the grant item key shape, and the updated Block
Kit copy. The handler also bundles cleanly with the same esbuild invocation
Pulumi uses.

## Still needs a human / decisions

- **No `pulumi`/apply in this container**, so CI is the proof. This PR needs a
  human on `@thegoodparty/gp-contrib` (every path here is owned).
- **The `sso-directory` dependent actions.** The AWS service authorization
  reference lists `sso-directory:GetUserId` and `sso-directory:IsMemberInGroups`
  as dependent actions of the two new `identitystore` calls, but the settled
  design and this task say to keep `sso-directory:*` absent. If the directory
  turns out to need them, `GetUserId`/`IsMemberInGroups` will fail closed with
  `AccessDenied`; the fix is one narrow `sso-directory:GetUserId` /
  `sso-directory:IsMemberInGroups` addition and should be a deliberate decision.
- **Identity Store region.** `sheriff/identity.ts` uses `us-west-2` for the
  `IdentitystoreClient` endpoint (Identity Store ARNs carry no region). If the
  management account's Identity Center instance lives elsewhere, that constant
  is the one line to change.
- **The SNS email subscription** stays unconfirmed until someone accepts the
  AWS email sent to `aws-infrastructure@goodparty.org`.
- **End-to-end test**: the flow has not been exercised against real Slack or
  Identity Center; that is the post-apply check.

---
> Brought to you by in silico Jeff (pi, deepseek-v4p1-flash)

priorFindings.body:
**`handleSweep` has no test coverage — critical lock-release and revoke-failure invariants are untested.**

`handleSweep` is never imported or invoked in any test file. The `reconcileSweep` tests (sheriff.test.ts lines 460–546) verify only the pure planning function; two non-trivial imperative paths are completely untested:

1. **`plan.failed` loop** (~lines 664–684): `releaseActiveGrant` is wrapped in `finally` so a failed `setGrantState` write cannot leave the at-most-one-active-grant lock stuck. No test verifies that `releaseActiveGrant` is called even when the preceding `setGrantState` throws.

2. **`plan.revoke` loop** (~lines 709–758): on a successful `deleteAdminsMembership` the lock is released in `finally`; on a failed delete the lock is intentionally *not* released (the membership still exists, so a second grant must stay blocked). This is a critical security invariant — if the `continue` or lock-retention logic were accidentally swapped, a revoke failure would release the lock and allow a second grant while the membership still exists. No test exercises either branch.

*(Falsification: searched all test files matching `sheriff*.test.*` for any reference to `handleSweep` — none found. The only other test file is `deploy/sheriff-grant.test.ts`, which covers a different module.)*

**`createAdminsMembership` still re-throws `ConflictException` when both fallback listings lag, leaving untracked Admins access.**

When `CreateGroupMembership` throws `ConflictException` (proving the user IS in Admins) but both `resolveAdminsMembershipId` (line 181) and `listAdminsMemberships` (line 191) return empty due to eventual-consistency lag, the code falls through to `throw err` at line 197. The handler (~line 435-443) transitions the grant to `failed` and releases the active-grant lock. The Admins membership now exists in AWS but is permanently untracked: `reconcileSweep` only processes `granting`/`granted` states (policy.ts lines 308, 321), and the sweeper explicitly never removes memberships with no active grant record (`membership.unmanaged`). No test covers the dual-lag scenario.

Consider throwing a distinct retriable error instead of re-throwing `ConflictException`, so the caller can distinguish this edge case and avoid marking the grant as permanently failed.

*(Falsification: confirmed `reconcileSweep` iterates only `granting`/`granted` states; a `failed` grant with a live Admins membership has no recovery path. The second fallback via `listAdminsMemberships` was added since the prior finding but does not close the window when both listings lag.)*
